title: King Oliver's baby cry and Robert Taylor's preaching trumpet
summary: Miller has not heard Oliver do the crying baby but describes Robert Taylor's preaching call-and-response trumpet.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: You know what I mean? All the movies. King Oliver and everybody else. Stuff they played. Everybody played. But behind them, they didn't care. Everything they played. Yeah, brother.

Well, Joe Oliver never put a lot of his baby in preaching and all that. You know, baby cry. He could make a baby cry with the trumpet, they say. And he never put that on the record. Well... He never preached on the record.
I don't know. I've never heard him do that.
You never heard him do that, huh? Well, I've heard talked about it.
I know that boy, Robert Taylor. He got that... Well, he kicked that woman. He got power. He could preach on the home.
How would he do that? What's that like? What's that like?
Well, I know he's... And the people would be saying, Yes, brother. And he'd be... He'd be making something people... Every time he'd make something like this, He'd say,
Yes, brother. Yeah, brother. Cut it. Well, brother, I guess, you know.
He'd be absolutely right. And he could do a lot of that. But he always hated singing, and nobody's gonna make it. What's that?
I didn't play that thing for you on that first night of him.
The piece I told you when I first used to play in racing now.
What's the name of the tune?
I don't know. It had no name. It goes in the mood, but it's not in the mood.
